title.narrative: UN Women Resilience to Disasters Programme in Malawi

description.narrative: The pilot disaster risk reduction and gender equality program in Malawi is designed to strengthen the capacities of duty bearers, communities and women led organisations to effectively adapt and respond to disasters and the impacts of climate change.

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: The UN Women, Women’s Resilience to Disasters Program sought to improve women’s resilience to natural disasters and climate threats in three districts in Malawi by supporting the development and adoption of gender responsive decision-making and governance systems on disaster risk reduction (DRR), enabling targeted action to build the resilience of women and girls. This was achieved through the implementation of gender-responsive preparedness and early warning systems, capacity development for women’s leadership in DRR organisations and development of gender responsive frameworks and provision of resilient business activities. For example, the Program contributed to development of the 2023-2024 Malawi National Multi Hazard Contingency Plan (NCP), ensuring a gender-responsive approach, including integrating gender considerations into the NCP, and addressing the unique challenges faced by women and marginalized groups during disasters. Since July 2023, a total of 11,643 people were directly involved in and benefited from program activities.

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: The Women’s Resilience to Disasters program is an investment in Malawi that is increasing women’s resilience to natural disasters and climate threats. The program is supporting the development and adoption of gender-responsive decision-making and governance systems for disaster risk reduction and enabling targeted action to build the resilience of women and girls in Malawi. The 2023–24 Malawi National Multi Hazard Contingency Plan was developed and adopted under this program. Deliberate efforts were taken to ensure the contingency plan was gender-responsive and addressed the unique challenges faced by women and marginalised groups during disasters. Since July 2023, a total of 11,643 people, including 9,058 women and 68 women with a disability were directly involved in and benefited from program activities.
